Ben Thompson on the two things Silicon Valley relearns every 10 years:

1) "Consumers do not want to pay for software"
2) "Consumers do not care about being productive"

"If you're going to be in the consumer market, you have to be doing advertising.

We went through this in early SaaS. The canonical company for this is Dropbox.

They had to rebuild the whole thing and realize the only way we're going to make money is by selling to companies.

You literally had OpenAI replaying the Dropbox story, but at like 100x the size.

We're going to sell subscriptions to consumers. And they did. They sold a lot, but they didn't sell enough.

If they had leaned into advertising immediately, as soon as ChatGPT was a hit, I think they would have a great ad product right now.

Charging people money is hard. Giving people things for free is easy."

Case in point: when models are asked to do too much tedious work, they are more likely to cheat.

A recent MATS paper demonstrated that if you ask Kimi K2 to fix a codebase with a large number of type errors, as the number of errors increases, the model becomes more likely to come up with a bullshit solution (i.e., just disable typechecking and not tell the user). This propensity increases linearly as the amount of work increases.

("But fixing 258 errors would be a huge task!")

So how do you deal with this? Kind of like how you'd deal with this with a human. If you asked a human to sit around doing tedious work for the next 8 hours, you would not expect a high degree of compliance. So instead, you should anticipate this and ask the model up front to divide up the work into fresh subagents that are less likely to get intimidated by the amount of work in front of it.

These techniques may eventually get upstreamed into the models themselves (Opus 6 will perhaps more naturally spin up subagents when presented with this task, anticipating its own tedium), but for now you, the model driver, still need to anticipat model psychology.

The Treasury’s larger long-end buybacks should ease pressure on long-term yields.

The Treasury will at least double buybacks across the 10-to-30-year sectors from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation beginning September 9. 

Funding for the buybacks comes through a broader borrowing program that leans on short-term bills. The net effect is a shift toward shorter maturities and less long-term debt for the market to absorb. This resembles one effect of QE even though the program is much smaller.

This matters because investors are demanding an unusually high premium to hold 10-year Treasuries relative to what the macro backdrop would normally justify. Expanded buybacks add another force pushing that premium and the 10-year yield lower.

Lower yields driven by a falling term premium have historically been constructive for risk assets. 

Suppressing the term premium while nominal growth remains near 6% shifts more inflation risk onto currency holders and could strengthen the case for gold and Bitcoin.

The case

Returns come from lending to real businesses, so they don't track crypto beta the way most of DeFi does. And private credit is illiquid by nature.

You can't sell a loan book same-day, so a redemption queue is the correct design rather than a flaw.

The risk

The instant withdrawal option barely works right now.

Midas is supposed to keep about 10% of the fund in cash so people can pull out immediately, which would be around $7M.

There's only $15.73K in there. So realistically you're joining the queue and waiting the 1 to 7 days, and Midas says the instant option is "indicative only" and can be switched off whenever anyway.

You're also taking their word on what the fund is worth. Fasanara's loan book isn't visible to anyone outside the fund…there's no version of this where you go check the positions yourself.

Mint avUSD with USDC, then stake into savUSD for the yield-bearing senior version

Avant runs it across lending, basis trades, Pendle, liquidity provision $127M avUSD TVL

The case

The tranche structure. $16.77M sits in front of savUSD holders and absorbs losses first, roughly 13% of the book.

You are not the doer. There is no individual entity doing anything.

Everything simply happens.

If you are truly the thinker, stop thinking for five minutes. You cannot. Thoughts keep appearing.

So where is the thinker?

Even the thought “I did this” appears after the action has already happened. The action comes first. Then the mind claims ownership.

Events happen. Deeds are done. There is no individual doer thereof.

When you believe “I am the doer,” success creates pride, failure creates guilt, and life becomes a struggle to control what cannot be controlled.

When non-doership is understood, life continues. You work. You speak. You love. You decide. Only the burden becomes lighter.

But where is the past except as memory appearing now? Where is the future except as imagination appearing now?

Both are thoughts happening now.

There is only this moment.

Every organism acts according to conditioning. Your genes, upbringing, experiences, and circumstances shape how you respond.

Did you choose your genes? Your parents? The experiences that shaped you? No. The conditioning was given.

Look at any decision. Options appeared as thoughts. Preferences arose according to conditioning. One became stronger. Action happened.

Where is the separate entity exercising completely independent free will?

There is only cause and effect functioning through the organism.

You find thoughts, sensations, memories, feelings. But where is the owner?

The “me” is another thought claiming ownership of experience.

There is no separate person who becomes enlightened. There is simply understanding.

Do not try to become “someone who is not the doer.” That is the ego playing another game.

Non-doership is not an achievement. It is seeing that there never was an independent doer.

Life continues. Work, love, pain, pleasure, laughter, disappointment.

Peace is not permanent pleasure. Peace is the absence of the mind’s demand that life must be different.

You did not write the script. You are not directing every scene.

Life lives itself.

There is nowhere to arrive. No one to become.

Only this moment.

And underneath all the noise, the peace that was always here.

You are not the doer. There is no individual entity doing anything.

Everything simply happens.

Look right now. The hand moves. The eyes blink. The heart beats. The breath flows. Did you consciously command any of it? Are you breathing, or is breathing simply happening?

Now observe a thought. Did you create it? Did you know what the next thought would be before it appeared?

If you are truly the thinker, stop thinking for five minutes. You cannot. Thoughts keep appearing.

So where is the thinker?

Even the thought “I did this” appears after the action has already happened. The action comes first. Then the mind claims ownership.

Events happen. Deeds are done. There is no individual doer thereof.

When you believe “I am the doer,” success creates pride, failure creates guilt, and life becomes a struggle to control what cannot be controlled.

When non-doership is understood, life continues. You work. You speak. You love. You decide. Only the burden becomes lighter.

Call it God, Consciousness, Source or life. The name does not matter. The body mind organism is simply an instrument through which life functions.

Thought creates psychological time.

A thought about the past appears, and the past seems to exist. A thought about the future appears, you believe it, and suddenly the future seems real.

But where is the past except as memory appearing now? Where is the future except as imagination appearing now?

Both are thoughts happening now.

There is only this moment.

Every organism acts according to conditioning. Your genes, upbringing, experiences, and circumstances shape how you respond.

Did you choose your genes? Your parents? The experiences that shaped you? No. The conditioning was given.

Look at any decision. Options appeared as thoughts. Preferences arose according to conditioning. One became stronger. Action happened.

Where is the separate entity exercising completely independent free will?

There is only cause and effect functioning through the organism.

If there is no independent doer, guilt and pride lose their foundation. Failure happens and the ego says, “I failed.” Success happens and the ego says, “I did it.”

The same applies to others. They too act according to conditioning they did not choose. This does not mean accepting harmful behavior. You can act, leave, defend yourself, or impose consequences. But hatred becomes less necessary. Understanding gives rise to compassion.

Even the spiritual search is not yours. The interest appeared. The teacher appeared. The question appeared. You did not decide to seek. Seeking happened.

Now look for the separate self.

You find thoughts, sensations, memories, feelings. But where is the owner?

The “me” is another thought claiming ownership of experience.

There is no separate person who becomes enlightened. There is simply understanding.

Do not try to become “someone who is not the doer.” That is the ego playing another game.

Non-doership is not an achievement. It is seeing that there never was an independent doer.

Life continues. Work, love, pain, pleasure, laughter, disappointment.

Peace is not permanent pleasure. Peace is the absence of the mind’s demand that life must be different.

You did not write the script. You are not directing every scene.

Life lives itself.

There is nowhere to arrive. No one to become.

Only this moment.

And underneath all the noise, the peace that was always here.

Radical transparency forces issues to the surface—most importantly (and most uncomfortably) the problems that people are dealing with and how they’re dealing with them—and it allows the organization to draw on the talents and insights of all its members to solve them. Eventually, for people who get used to it, living in a culture of radical transparency is more comfortable than living in the fog of not knowing what’s going on and not knowing what people really think. And it is incredibly effective. 

But, to be clear, like most great things it also has drawbacks. Its biggest drawback is that it is initially very difficult for most people to deal with uncomfortable realities. If unmanaged, it can lead to people getting involved with more things than they should, and can lead people who aren’t able to weigh all the information to draw the wrong conclusions. #principleoftheday
